diagram_math_checks.result: All four objects are C^N for N>=1. The zero-based vectors (x_0,...,x_{N-1}) identify with functions on Z/NZ via the standard representatives. def-unitary-discrete-fourier-transform-on-z-mod-n defines F_N as an endomorphism on those functions, hence C^N under this identification. def-toeplitz-circulant-and-displacement-notation defines C(c)_{ij}=c_{(i-j) mod N}, so the upper map is C^N -> C^N. The lower diag(lambda_0,...,lambda_{N-1}) is also C^N -> C^N.

diagram_math_checks.check: DFT sign, normalization and eigenvalue indexing
diagram_math_checks.result: The DFT definition uses N^(-1/2) sum_{j=0}^{N-1} x_j exp(-2 pi i k j/N). Thus lambda_k=sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j exp(-2 pi i k j/N)=sqrt(N)(F_N c)(k), for 0<=k<N exactly as in the Statement; the inversion supplier uses the positive sign with the same N^(-1/2) factor.

Both horizontal arrows point right; both vertical arrows point down and are F_N. Proof step 1.1 identifies C(c)x with cyclic convolution. The full local convolution supplier proof reindexes z=x-y and factors the negative-sign exponential, giving F_N(c*x)=sqrt(N)(F_N c) odot(F_N x). Consequently each k coordinate of the upper-then-right-vertical path is lambda_k(F_N x)(k), equal to the left-vertical-then-lower path; this is exactly proof step 2.1. No inverse transform belongs on the downward arrows.

Proof steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 establish the matrix identity, diagonalization and solvability directly from finite sums and Fourier inversion without invoking the square. Only the unsupported label command changes.
